slides.title: How to Get Barakah Back in Your Mornings
slides.sub: Swipe for the du'a the Prophet ﷺ made for the early morning, what he did after Fajr, and 3 small changes for tomorrow.
slides.by: A letter from The Tazkiyyah Guide

blocks: "Why is half my day gone before it starts?"
"Why do I wake up already tired?"
"Why does nothing I start ever stick?"
Often it isn't your schedule. It's your first hour.
When we talk about barakah, we mean blessing from Allah.
It's when a little does a lot.
Two rak'ahs that settle your whole heart.
An hour of work that does the job of three.
A small income that somehow covers everything.
You can't buy it. You can't hustle for it.
But the Prophet ﷺ told us where to look for it:
the early morning.
He ﷺ made this du'a for us:
"O Allah, bless my ummah in their early mornings."
When he sent out an army, he sent it at the start of the day.
Sakhr, the companion who narrated it, was a merchant.
He sent his goods out at the start of the day, and he became rich and had much wealth.
Same 24 hours as everyone else.
A different first hour.
He ﷺ asked Allah to bless that hour for you.
The only question is whether you're awake for it.

slides.after: If you change only one thing, keep your phone out of reach until your adhkar are done.

blocks: ## What he ﷺ did after Fajr
Jabir ibn Samurah reported that when the Prophet ﷺ prayed Fajr, he would sit in his place until the sun had risen. *(Sahih Muslim 670)*
He didn't rush into the day. He stayed with Allah first.
So here are 3 small changes for tomorrow:
**1.** Charge your phone outside your room.
**2.** After Fajr, stay seated for your adhkar, even for ten minutes.
**3.** Do your hardest task before you open a single app.
Don't try all three at once.
Pick one and keep it for a week.
Barakah grows in what you keep doing.
Tomorrow's Fajr is the first test.
